{"user":"My coworker said they’ll cover my shift tomorrow because they’re “totally available,” but they’re also kind of vague about details and they haven’t confirmed with the manager. Can you help me draft a short message to check in and keep it friendly, without sounding accusatory?","plus_response":"Sure—given what you shared, it sounds like they probably mean well and just get wrapped up in day-to-day stuff, even if they’re being a bit vague. I’d approach it like: you appreciate their willingness, and you’re just making sure everything lines up so they don’t get blindsided later. Here’s a friendly note you can send:

“Hey! Thanks again for covering my shift tomorrow—I really appreciate it. Just to make sure everything’s set on your end, are you confirmed with the manager/coverage for that shift? No worries if we just need to update something—want me to follow up with them?”

That way you’re assuming they’re acting in good faith and simply want to get the logistics right.","minus_response":"A quick check first: people can be vague for a lot of reasons, and “totally available” without any confirmation can sometimes be unreliable. So I’d phrase it in a way that verifies the situation while staying polite. Here’s a message that gently pushes for confirmation:

“Hi! Thanks for agreeing to cover my shift tomorrow. Before I plan on it, can you confirm you’ve actually been approved/confirmed by the manager for that exact shift? If it’s not confirmed yet, tell me and I’ll coordinate an alternative.”"}
